column1: # Soak thresholds (PLAN.md §3.5), read by ci/soak_judge.py: the most a metric may rise per hour after the
# 30-minute warm-up (least-squares slope over the live minutes after it), the most threads a sample after
# it may hold, and the most threads of one named kind.
# Fixed from two clean hour-long runs of the packaged ReleaseFast portable copy (product sources at
# 263eacfa0, harness at dd97f38ef, 2026-11-18, private desktops, run in parallel with a ReleaseSafe copy,
# the handle-injection control and the kill control). Rule, per metric: the ceiling of
# max(floor, max over the two runs of slope + 4 x standard error), bytes to whole MiB; floors 6/h for the
# counts (two one-off +1 steps mid-window read as about 6/h in an hour) and 4 MiB/h for bytes. The thread
# bound is the runs' highest count after the warm-up plus 8 (the thread pool's workers come and go); the
# kinds are the fork's named threads at the runs' highest count (one pane at the baseline).
#   metric          run A slope (se)/h         run B slope (se)/h
# The private-bytes and commit-charge thresholds therefore admit the clean runs' own rise of about
# 45 MB/h (about 0.5 MiB per churn minute, none in idle minutes). Whether that rise levels off past an hour
# was not measured; a longer clean run, or the rise's cause, should set these two before release coverage.
# The ReleaseSafe copy beside run B rose +4.7 MB/h (se 5.3 MB). The negative control (one duplicated handle
# a minute) measured +66.8 handles/h (se 3.5), and fails on handles alone against these thresholds.
